title: ArcelorMittal Halts Ukraine's Second-Largest Steel Plant in Kryvyi Rih After Repeated Russian Strikes
detail: ArcelorMittal announced it has completely halted operations at its Kryvyi Rih steel plant — Ukraine's second-largest steelmaker and President Zelenskyy's hometown — after four Russian missile strikes over the past five weeks killed 5 and injured 17, most recently on September 21. CEO Mauro Longobardo said the company "concluded that we are no longer able to safely operate ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih." The plant produced 1.7 million tons of steel (23% of Ukraine's output) and 1.6 million tons of rolled products (24% of national output) in 2025, generating Hr. 70.6 billion ($1.6B) in revenue against a Hr. 8.9 billion ($199M) net loss. ArcelorMittal expects to book a roughly $1 billion non-cash impairment charge and will not resume operations until the war ends. With ArcelorMittal's shutdown, all three of Ukraine's major steel plants — together accounting for about 90% of national steel production — have now halted operations.

title: Russia Claims Strikes on Kyiv Data Center and Odessa Infrastructure
detail: Russia claimed strikes against a data center in Kyiv and infrastructure in the Odessa region on September 26, per Le Monde's live war blog. The Russian Defense Ministry said its forces targeted the data center facility in the Ukrainian capital and energy or logistics infrastructure in the Odessa area. Ukraine has not yet confirmed damage. The strikes follow a pattern of Russian attacks targeting Ukraine's digital and critical infrastructure, including two nights of Kyiv missile and drone strikes earlier in the week.

title: China Reveals Peace Plan to End Russia's War Against Ukraine
detail: China unveiled a peace plan aimed at ending Russia's war against Ukraine, signaling a notable shift in Beijing's public diplomatic posture on the conflict. The proposal represents a more active Chinese role in seeking a resolution after years of maintaining studied ambiguity between supporting Russia economically while nominally calling for peace. Details of the plan were not immediately specified, but the move comes as both sides show no near-term willingness to negotiate, with Lavrov declaring the war will continue 'through to the end' on the same day.

title: Lavrov: Russia's War in Ukraine Will Continue 'Through to the End'
detail: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov declared on September 26 that Russia's war in Ukraine will continue 'through to the end,' dashing any near-term ceasefire hopes. The statement came as China announced a peace plan and Ukraine and its allies announced plans for additional pressure measures. Lavrov's comments reaffirm Russia's maximalist war aims and signal no imminent willingness to enter good-faith negotiations, consistent with Moscow's refusal to accept any ceasefire terms that would require withdrawal from occupied Ukrainian territories.

title: Zelensky: Russia Shows No Readiness to End War as Ukraine Plans Additional Pressure
detail: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on September 26 that Russia shows no readiness to end the war, as Ukraine and its allies plan additional pressure measures against Moscow. Zelensky's assessment came on the same day that Lavrov declared the war would continue 'through to the end' and China announced a peace plan. Ukraine and Western partners are reportedly coordinating further sanctions and military aid packages aimed at increasing the cost of Russia's continued aggression and forcing a shift in Moscow's calculus.
